gaps: Earliest dated use of 誰 as an interrogative pronoun was not established. The sources inspected quote the received 說文 gloss and later classical examples but do not date the earliest surviving inscription or textual witness.

CUHK interprets bronze 誰 as originally ‘dark horse’ (騅) and reports a bronze use of bare 隹 for the interrogative 誰. These claims suggest graphic/sense history, but the inspected material does not independently establish how the horse-name was pronounced or prove a sound-based borrowing from that name. Do not treat the reconstruction of the pronoun alone as evidence for the horse's name pronunciation.

No oracle-bone form is listed by the inspected CUHK entry; absence from that entry does not prove the graph was absent from all oracle-bone material. The exact dates and provenance of the cited bronze artifacts were not verified.

The semantic path from the reported horse sense to the interrogative pronoun, and the relative chronology of the bare 隹 and 言+隹 uses, need primary inscription editions or specialist paleographic discussion beyond the inspected page.

The simplified counterpart relation 誰 → 谁 is present in the dossier's imported record, but the inspected sources here did not provide an explicit source statement establishing this standardization; component-level origin classification should therefore remain uncertain absent a supporting citation. The visible 言-side shorthand 讠 is not separately evidenced in the opened sources.

The official Unicode Unihan character records could not be accessed through the web tool. Local supplied rows report the readings, but are local data, not verified external pages; no supplied local row gives 隹's reading.
No exact local Baxter–Sagart row for 隹 was supplied. Consequently, the provided local table permits reporting 誰's MC dzywij and OC *[d]uj, but not a same-system host-versus-component comparison.

The CUHK site is repeatedly useful across character research, but no reuse license for its character-specific entries or bulk text was verified. Recommend citation and paraphrase only, not a tracked extract.
The earliest dated attestation of 誰 as an interrogative pronoun was not established. The inspected sources quote 說文 and cite later received texts, but no dated earliest witness was verified.

The CUHK entry proposes that the bronze graph 誰 first meant a dark horse and says a bronze inscription form is read as 騅. The horse-name’s original pronunciation was not independently established here. A reconstruction for the pronoun alone does not demonstrate the name or pronunciation of the horse, so the proposed relation must not be presented as a proven sound-based borrowing.

The reported Zhongshan bronze use of bare 隹 for 誰 supports a reading of that inscription, but the sources inspected do not settle whether it represents a whole graph used for the pronoun, the relative chronology of that use and 言+隹, or the semantic path from a proposed horse sense.

The CUHK 誰 entry lists no oracle-bone example. That is evidence about the entry’s coverage, not proof that no oracle-bone form exists. Exact artifact provenance and dates for the cited bronze forms were not verified.

The opened Ministry of Education entry presents 誰 and cites uses, but does not explicitly document the standardization relation 誰 → 谁 or the component simplification 言 → 讠. Treat the dossier’s simplification note as an imported assertion, not newly verified evidence.

The exact official Unicode Unihan records for 誰 and 隹 were inaccessible to the web tool. The supplied local 誰 row is shuí shéi; no supplied local 隹 row is available. No same-system Baxter–Sagart comparison between host and component is established by this packet.

No usable, character-specific historical glyph image with inspected identity and reuse provenance was established. Generic or unrelated Commons results cannot support an image choice; the Academia Sinica CC0 notice is general and does not substitute for an inspected 誰 query record. No glyph was visually inspected.
The repeatedly useful CUHK character page has no verified reuse license in the material inspected. Cite and paraphrase its entry; no local extract is recommended.

The Zhongshan inscription article could not be opened; its search-result transcription should not be treated as verified page content. A directly inspected inscription edition is still needed to substantiate the bare-隹 reading externally in this pass.

The exact local Baxter–Sagart rows establish the separate readings for 誰 and 隹 in MC and OC notation, but the search did not locate or inspect the original table online. The comparison does not prove a sound-component role or a whole-graph borrowing.

The official Unihan character pages for 誰 and 隹 could not be accessed. Their supplied local kMandarin rows are available, but an externally inspected character-specific Unicode record and click-through citation remain unverified.

The search surfaced simplified-form identification for 誰 → 谁 and the local dossier states 訁 → 讠, but no primary standardization source was successfully opened. The literal component pair 訁 → 讠 is not the same pair as 言 → 讠.

No independently inspected source establishes the pronunciation of the proposed horse-name 騅. Reconstructions of 誰 and 隹 cannot by themselves establish the horse name’s pronunciation or a sound-based borrowing from it.

The earliest dated attestation of 誰 as an interrogative pronoun, precise dates/provenance of cited bronze forms, semantic extensions’ chronology, and transitions between interrogative, assertive ‘anyone’, and rhetorical uses remain unresolved.

The Palace Museum article's search snippet explicitly reads the bronze graph as 隹(谁), but the PDF could not be opened and the Fudan article inspected does not discuss that passage. The opened inscription transcription gives 谁 but not the graph's original shape; the bare-隹 reading therefore remains supported by the earlier CUHK dictionary report in the dossier, but was not independently confirmed from a newly opened inscription edition here.

Exact official Unicode kMandarin pages for 誰 (U+8AB0), 谁 (U+8C01), and 隹 (U+96B9) were not successfully inspected. The exact supplied local rows are recorded separately and should not be passed off as page-verified external data.

The exact Baxter–Sagart rows for both 誰 and 隹 were supplied locally and checked; no publicly accessible original table page with those exact rows was inspected. The local reading data support the same-system comparison only, not phonetic-role proof.
The local search hint for Shuowen Seal Radical 109 was not opened; the directly verified 隹-seal.svg asset is the selected suitable component illustration instead.
